Item: Tomo by DreamMachina (formerly evoKin V.01) — bill of materials, V.01 lighter Tomo / Mirumi look (passive spring hug)
Notes: Prices in AUD from November 2026 supplier quotes and may have changed. Internal file names keep the evokin_ prefix.

Item: Feetech FS90 plastic-gear micro servo, 9 g (head pan, in the yaw collar) — was FS90MG
Notes: Lighter Tomo: 9 g vs 13.4 g for the FS90MG. Same 22.5×12.1×22.4 case per the Feetech spec sheet (https://www.feetech.cn/en/6v-15kg-9g-dc-reduction-steering-gear-tooth-box; PDF https://www.feetech.cn/Data/feetechrc/upload/file/20200612/6372758162968290344365716.pdf), so it drops into the FS90MG seat (Pololu lists 23.2×12.5×22: check on arrival). 1.3 kg·cm @4.8 V / 1.5 @6 V, stall 700/800 mA, 21T spline. Software clamp ±42°, printed hard stop ≈ ±47°. Plastic gears: the head is moved by the servo only, nothing hangs off it.

Item: Feetech FS90 plastic-gear micro servo, 9 g (head tilt / nod, on the neck turret) — was FS90MG
Notes: See M1. Tilt axis along x through y=6, z=119; software clamp ±10°. The lighter head (≈38 g) with its COM close to the axis loads the FS90 to a few % of stall (results/metrics_v01.json). Back-drive of the plastic gear train if the face is pushed hard is the main risk: the head is a nod, not a handle.

Item: Music-wire torsion spring, 0.048 in (1.22 mm) wire, 3/8 in OD, 90° legs, LEFT-hand wound — Approved Vendor / Grainger 3HPG6 (6-pack), for the left shoulder
Notes: Rated 2.679 lbf·in (302.7 N·mm) at 90° → 3.36 N·mm/°. Preload 30° at the rest stop, 90° at the 60° open stop (exactly the 90° catalogue rating, no margin; a spring rated past 90° would add margin). PRICE UNCERTAIN: Raptor Supplies AU showed A$16.98 per 6-pack on the category page but about A$108–109 on the product page (Nov 2026). Confirm before ordering; not in the totals. Check winding hand against the CAD before ordering.

Item: Same torsion spring, RIGHT-hand wound — Approved Vendor / Grainger 3HPD1 (6-pack), for the right shoulder
Notes: See M3. One pack of each hand gives 5 spares per side for tuning; a weaker or stronger spring changes pad force in proportion (≈3.2–3.7 N per arm with this one).

Item: M3 × 30 screw (shoulder hinge pin, thread-formed into the torso ear) + M3 washer + M3 nyloc nut, one set per arm
Notes: Ø2.5 thread-forming pilot in the torso ear and spigot; Ø3.4 running bore in the knuckle (z 70–86). Washer + nyloc under the knuckle, snug not tight. There is no lower hip cap any more. Confirm length on the printed stack.

Item: (removed) M2.5 hip-cap screws — the hip caps are gone in the Mirumi-proportion pass
Notes: The arms hang from the shoulder ear on the pin alone, so the arm band can leave the knuckle downwards.

Notes: The screw listed with the servo is M2.5×4, too short for a 2.0 mm horn + printed part + thread. Measure the included horns and screws on arrival.

Item: M2 self-tapping screws, tilt_hub to the tilt horn (2) + 1 key screw into head_back
Notes: Pilots Ø1.7 at an ASSUMED r=7 mm on the horn; drill to suit the horn that arrives.

Item: M3 × 12 thread-forming screw, tilt idler pivot (head_back boss on the neck_turret column)
Notes: Ø2.5 pilot in the turret column, clearance in the head boss. Do not overtighten: it is the second tilt bearing.

Item: M2.5 screws (clearance 2.8 mm in the front/through half, pilot 2.1 mm in the back/receiving half). Torso 4 + head 4 + collar 4
Notes: Optional M2.5 heat-set inserts later; bosses are Ø7. The shoulder-cap screws of the clasp design are gone.

Item: M2 screws for yaw retainers (clearance 2.3 mm in the retainer, pilot 1.7 mm in the neck_turret skirt)
Servo-tab self-tappers (or M2) into 1.7 mm printed pilots, 2 per servo
Status: Confirm on arrival — may be included with the servos
Notes: 2 servos in V.01 (pan + tilt). PDF p.6 is a blank “No Accessories” sheet; product pages usually include screws.

Item: Fur skin: long dense pile (≈15–18 mm guard hair, ~8 mm undercoat) on the body; two short, thick, symmetric stuffed arm sleeves (Ø16–18 mm tube before pile, ≈Ø26–28 mm with it, ≈55 mm along the spine) with a shoulder cap over each knuckle and a rounded mitten paw, the two mittens flattened where they meet in front of the handle; two stubby plush feet. Proxies in stl/reference/ (fur_proxy_torso, sleeve_proxy_L/R)
Notes: Mirumi look: ivory (hero) or pink. ASSUMED 21 g body skin + feet, plus ≈1 g extra pile for the thicker arm tubes (380 g/m²). Arm sleeves: sew each as a fur tube with a closed mitten end, slide over the printed spine, stuff lightly (M20) and close at the shoulder cap, which is sewn to the body skin over the knuckle. Leave a slot on the inner face of each mitten so the fur-coloured TPU pad (M14) touches the handle; the pile hides it. Face-cap lip over the z≈101 seam, trimmed eye/nose wells, vertical channel (or slit) down the centre of the belly for the handle upright.

Item: TPU pads (stl/paw_pad_L.stl, paw_pad_R.stl), 1.5 mm sleeves over the paw ends of the arms (in front of the handle), 85A–95A
Notes: Glue or stretch on. They take the squash on the handle (the rigid arm stays ≈1.4 mm clear) and give the grip friction (μ ≈ 0.5 assumed). Dye or print in a fur-matched TPU: they sit on the underside of the arm sleeves and are hidden by the pile.

Item: Printed yaw thrust washer (stl/yaw_thrust_washer.stl); 0.8 mm, ID 35, OD 43
Notes: Print flat on the bed, no supports. Designed 0.30 mm axial gap under the turret cone.

Item: Optional test coupon (stl/coupon.stl)
Status: Print first if you print at all
Notes: Journal + skirt (0.35 mm radial) + washer, tab/pocket, and an FS90/FS90MG seat (same case). A passing coupon is not a full fit-check.

Item: Adafruit 3923 Mini Oval Speaker, 8 Ω 1 W, 30×20×5 mm, 3 g — was the 25 g Adafruit 3351 enclosure
Supplier: Core Electronics (ADA3923) — out of stock Nov 2026
Notes: Core page https://core-electronics.com.au/mini-oval-speaker-8-ohm-1-watt.html. Adafruit lists 3 g (an older PDF says 1.4 g). Sits in a printed frame on the inside of torso_back (centre x0 y38 z64), firing through a 5×3 grid of Ø2.2 grille holes. Quieter than the 3351: the MAX98357A puts ≈1.4 W into 8 Ω at 5 V, so set the gain low (1 W speaker).

Item: 8 mm black safety eyes with push-on washers (replace the printed bezels and shutter)
Notes: Shank through Ø5.0 holes at x ±10.5, z 114 in head_front; ≈0.4 g each. Small and low and close like Mirumi's bead eyes. Toy-safety-rated washers if anyone small handles it.

Item: 1S LiPo 3.7 V 400 mAh, 38×25×6 mm, 11 g, JST-PH, built-in PCM — was a 2000 mAh 1S (≈38 g)
Notes: 2C continuous (0.8 A), wiring/connector rated 1 A. Two FS90 stalling together draw ≈1.4 A at 5 V (≈2 A from the cell): the firmware moves one servo at a time and the INA219 trip must stay under the cell limit. ≈2 h at ~170 mA average (Wi-Fi + idle servos), less with streaming. Charged by the XIAO's onboard charger.

Item: Polyester fibrefill (toy stuffing) for the two arm sleeves
Notes: ≈32 cm³ of sleeve less the printed spines, at an ASSUMED 15 kg/m³ loosely packed (≈0.5 g). Keep it loose so the mittens squash round the handle and against each other.

Item: Seeed Studio XIAO ESP32S3 Sense (brain + OV3660/OV5640 camera + PDM mic + LiPo charger)
Notes: 21×17.5 mm, ≈6.6 g with the Sense board (Seeed). Seeed now ships OV3660/OV5640 (OV2640 discontinued). The camera is removed from the Sense board and run on a long 24-pin FPC to the 'nose' pod in head_front (lens behind a Ø3.5 window at z 110); optional: leave it unplugged to save ≈1 g and power. Price as quoted Nov 2026.

Item: ESP32-S3-WROOM-1U-N16R8 module (U.FL, 16 MB flash, 8 MB Octal PSRAM) for a later custom board
Notes: LCSC equivalent C3013946. Four modules are a project buy, not a per-robot quantity. DigiKey line with A1 is about A$66.50 with free shipping (Nov 2026 quote).

Item: MAX98357A I2S amplifier breakout (clone)
Notes: Name-brand alternative: Adafruit 3006 / Core Electronics about A$10.65. CAD pocket is 19.4×17.8×3.0 plus 8 mm terminal-block headroom; measure the board. With the 1 W 8 Ω speaker (M17) keep the gain at the lowest setting.

Item: INA219 current-sensor breakout (clone), for the 5 V servo rail
Notes: Used with a software trip plus an eFuse or load switch so the servo rail drops if the head stalls or is forced. The arms are passive now, so there is no grip current to cap. Measure the real servo current before setting the threshold. Name-brand Core price about A$17.30.

Item: Pololu U3V16F5 5 V step-up regulator, 0.4 g, 13.1×8.1×3 mm (servo rail) — was the XL6009 module
Notes: https://www.pololu.com/product/4941: 1.3–16 V in (2.7 V start-up), ≈1.6 A typical continuous input, so roughly 1 A at 5 V from a 3.7 V cell; over-temperature shutdown and input current limit, but no short-circuit or reverse protection. 33 µF on VIN and 470 µF on the 5 V servo header. Two servos must not stall together (see M19).

Item: TP4056 LiPo charger board
Notes: Many bare TP4056 boards have no protection IC. Use only a pack that already has a PCM, or prefer a BQ24074 power-path charger (Core breakout about A$28.25; also the custom-board target).

Item: DFRobot ESP32-S3 AI Camera (DFR1154): OV3660, PDM mic, MAX98357, 5–12 V VIN, no charger
Notes: Only GPIO43/44 (Gravity/UART port) are free on this board per the DFRobot wiki; everything else is used by camera, PDM mic, MAX98357, SD, IR LED, LED and BOOT. Those two pins could drive the two head servos directly, but then there is no I2C for the INA219. Plan: use 43/44 as I2C for a PCA9685 servo driver (B4) and the INA219 (B2).

Item: INA219 current-sensor breakout (same as A4)
Notes: See A4.

Item: Pololu U3V16F5 5 V boost (same as A5)
Notes: See A5. The DFR1154 has no charger; add one for the 400 mAh cell (M19).

Item: PCA9685 16-channel I2C PWM/servo driver breakout
Notes: Needed only on the DFR1154 route (only 2 free GPIOs, shared with the INA219 on I2C). Not needed on the XIAO route (pan D0, tilt D1).

Item: MAX98357A I2S amplifier breakout (name-brand)
Notes: Use instead of A3 if you prefer a known board.

Item: INMP441 I2S MEMS microphone breakout
Notes: The XIAO Sense and DFR1154 already have a mic. Needed for a custom board, or if you mount a snout mic on a JST-SH lead. Beware fake clone INMP441 modules.

Item: BQ24074 LiPo charger / power-path breakout
Notes: True DPPM load sharing, unlike a basic TP4056. Also the charger IC on the custom-board target.

Item: Pololu S13V20F5 5 V 2 A+ regulator for the servo rail
Notes: Protected, higher-current alternative to the U3V16F5 (heavier: ≈1.3 g, larger).

Item: INA219 current-sensor breakout (name-brand)
Notes: Use instead of A4 if you prefer a known board.

Notes: 65×55 mm, 4-layer, single-sided SMT. Rough JLCPCB cost for 5 boards and 2 assembled is about A$120 including freight to Sydney (Gemini estimate, Nov 2026). Prefer TPS61088 over MT3608.
